title: Completeness and Cost of Retrieval Structures for Multi-Tool Requests in LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.41905v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: An agent that must call several tools to fulfill a request fails when the tool retriever omits any one of them, yet tool retrievers are mostly built and evaluated on queries requiring a single tool. We compare representatives of six retrieval structures (flat lexical and dense retrieval, LLM query decomposition, LLM-navigated hierarchies, server-then-tool matching, dependency graphs, and trained set-level retrievers) across two multi-tool testbeds: 345 AppWorld queries with expert dependency labels and 103 MCP-Bench tasks over 257 MCP tools. We measure completeness@k, the share of queries whose entire required tool set appears in the top k, alongside the LLM calls, tokens, and latency that each structure incurs at retrieval time. A motivating analysis on all 7,961 ToolRet queries shows that aggregate completeness mixes two regimes: completeness at 10 is .58 to .67 on single-target queries and .08 to .17 on queries with four or more tar

translated_title: LLM智能体中多工具请求的检索结构完整性与成本研究
translated_abstract: 当一个智能体需要调用多个工具才能完成某个请求时，只要工具检索器遗漏了其中任何一个工具，任务就会失败；然而，工具检索器大多是在仅需单个工具的查询上构建和评估的。我们在两个多工具测试平台上比较了六种检索结构的代表性方法（扁平词法与稠密检索、LLM查询分解、LLM导航的层次结构、先匹配服务器再匹配工具、依赖图以及经过训练的集合级检索器）：一个是带有专家依赖标注的345条AppWorld查询，另一个是覆盖257个MCP工具的103个MCP-Bench任务。我们测量completeness@k，即完整所需工具集全部出现在前k个检索结果中的查询占比，同时测量每种结构在检索时产生的LLM调用次数、token数量和延迟。针对全部7,961条ToolRet查询的动机性分析表明，总体完整性指标混合了两种不同情况：单目标查询在k=10时的完整性为0.58至0.67，而需要四个及以上工具的查询仅为0.08至0.17。
tldr: 该论文提出completeness@k指标，系统比较了六种工具检索结构在多工具请求下的完整性与检索成本，发现现有在单工具查询上构建的检索器在需要四个及以上工具的查询上性能急剧下降（完整性从0.58–0.67跌至0.08–0.17）。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the completeness@k metric and systematically compares six retrieval structures for multi-tool requests in LLM agents, revealing that retrievers built on single-tool queries suffer a sharp drop in completeness (from 0.58–0.67 to 0.08–0.17) when queries require four or more tools, while incurring varying costs in LLM calls, tokens, and latency.
